MC38, D4M.3 A, Panc02, mouse pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and human patient-derived PDAC cells were cultured in DMEM (Thermo Fisher Scientific) supplemented with 10% FCS, 50 U ml–1 penicillin and 50 mg ml–1 streptomycin. Gpx4−/− cells were cultured in their respective medium supplemented with 1 μM Lip-1 to prevent ferroptosis. For in vitro assays, Gpx4−/− cell lines were cultivated in 1 µM Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) for one passage before seeding them with or without Fer-1 to assess ferroptosis and PGE2 production. Unless stated otherwise, all analyses of cell viability and PGE2 production were performed after 24 h.

To generate cancer cell conditioned medium, 4 × 105 cancer cells were cultured in 2 ml complete RPMI medium or DMEM for 24 h before addition of the ferroptosis inducers RSL3 or ML210 (250 nM for NRAS(G12D), 500 nM for 4T1 and D4M.3A, and 1,000 nM for BRAF(V600E) and MC38 cells), doxorubicin (10 µM) or treatment with 150 mJ cm−2 UVB. 8 h later, cancer cells were washed three times with PBS and cultivated for another 16 h in complete RPMI or DMEM. The cell supernatant was collected, centrifuged at 600g for 5 min to remove dead cell debris and stored at −20 °C until further use. All cell lines were routinely tested for mycoplasma contamination in-house by PCR. No further cell line authentications were conducted in the laboratory.

Cancer cell lines were detached by trypsinization (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and washed three times in sterile PBS (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Cells were injected subcutaneously in 100 μl endotoxin-free PBS on the flank of recipient mice, using 2 × 105 cells for tumour growth studies and 2 × 106 cells for all other experiments. Tumour growth was measured using a digital calliper. Tumour diameters stated in the figures refer to the average values of the longest diameter and its perpendicular for each tumour. Tumour growth was restricted to a maximum diameter of 15 mm, which served as the humane end point and was not exceeded in any of the experiments. For animals reaching the humane end point before the end of the observation period, the last measured tumour diameter was carried forwards to subsequent time points (last observation carried forwards). For experiments involving ferroptotic control or Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− BRAF(V600E)–OVA melanoma cells, cancer cells were pre-treated with 1 μM RSL3 for 8 h before subcutaneous injection of 1 × 106 cells in 100 μl of endotoxin-free PBS into the flank of recipient mice.

To deplete CD8+ T cells, mice received intraperitoneal injections of 100 µl anti-mouse CD8β antibody (200 µg per mouse; 53-5.8, BioXCell) every 5 days, beginning on day 1 following tumour cell inoculation.

In a recent development, treatment of mice bearing subcutaneous MC38 or control BRAF(V600E) tumours was initiated once tumours were palpable, on days 3–5 post-tumour cell transplantation. Solutions were prepared fresh every day. For induction of ferroptosis, mice received daily intraperitoneal injection of 40 mg kg−1 IKE dissolved in 55% PEG 300 (Sigma) and 45% PBS. Lyophilized CXB (MedChem) was weighed using a fine balance and made up in a 60:40 ratio of DMSO (1 part, Sigma)/PEG400 (5 parts, Sigma):dH2O. The final concentration was 6 mg ml−1, corresponding to a dose of 30 mg kg−1 delivered in a total volume of 100 µl per mouse. CXB was administered daily by oral gavage.

Tumours, lymph nodes or spleens of tumour cell-inoculated mice were collected at the indicated time points after cancer cell transplantation. Tumour or organ weight was measured using a microscale. For flow cytometry analysis, tumour samples were mechanically dissociated and digested with DNase I (100 µg ml–1, Merck) and collagenase IV (200 U ml–1, Thermo Fisher Scientific) for 40 min at 37 °C followed by filtration through a 70-µm and a 30-µm cell strainer (Miltenyi) and washing with FACS buffer (PBS with 1% FCS and 2 mM EDTA) to generate single-cell suspensions before proceeding with antibody-mediated staining. Spleens were passed through a 70-µm cell strainer, followed by red blood cell lysis with ACK-lysis buffer for 3 min and additional filtration using a 30-µm cell strainer. Lymph nodes were dissociated using a 30-µm cell strainer.

It has been revealed that the following antibodies and staining reagents were used for flow cytometry or cell sorting: fixable viability dye eFluor 450 (dilution: 1:1,000; Thermo Fisher Scientific); fixable viability dye APC-eF780 (1:2,000; Thermo Fisher Scientific); PE-Cy7 anti-CD8α (1:200; 53-6.7, BioLegend); PE-Dazzle594 anti-CD8α (1:200; 53-6.7, BioLegend); BV711 anti-mouse/human-CD44 (1:100; IM7, BioLegend); PerCP-Cy5.5 anti-mouse/human-CD44 (1:100; IM7, BioLegend); PE anti-CD45.1 (1:100; A20, BioLegend); BV510 anti-CD45.2 (1:100; 104, BD Biosciences); BUV395 anti-CD45.2 (1:100; 104, BD Biosciences); FITC anti-CD62L (1:100; MEL-14, BioLegend); FITC anti-CD103 (1:100; M290, BD Biosciences); Pe-Cy7 anti-CD103 (1:100; 2E7; BioLegend); PE-Dazzle594 anti-CD186/CXCR6 (1:200; SA051D1, BioLegend); BV421 anti-CD366/TIM-3 (1:200; RMT3-23, BioLegend); BV605 anti-CD279/PD-1 (1:100; 29F.1A12, BioLegend); PerCP/Cy5.5 anti-TCRβ (1:100; H57-597, BioLegend); AF700 anti-TCRβ (1:100; H57-597, Sony); APC anti-human GZMB (1:200; GB12, Thermo Fisher Scientific); PE anti-human GZMB (1:200; GB12; Thermo Fisher Scientific); FITC anti-Ki-67 (1:100; SolA-15, Thermo Fisher Scientific); PE anti-mouse TCF1 (1:200; S33-966, BD Biosciences); and rabbit-anti-mouse-TCF1/TCF7 (1:100; C.725.7, Thermo Fisher Scientific). This was followed by staining with AF647 donkey-anti-rabbit IgG (1:200; Poly4064, BioLegend); BV605 anti-CD11b (1:200; M1/70; BioLegend); PerCP-Cy5.5 anti-CD11c (1:200; N418; BioLegend); PE-Cy7 anti-CD11c (1:200; M17/4; BioLegend); BV421 anti-XCR1 (1:200; ZET; BioLegend); PE anti-CXCL9 (1:100; MIG-2F5.5, BioLegend); PerCP/Cy5.5 anti-IL-12/IL-23 p40 (1:100; C15.6, BioLegend); FITC anti-I-A/I-E (MHC class II) (1:1,000; M5/114.15.2, Thermo Fisher Scientific); AF700 anti-mouse H-2kb (1:100; AF6-88.5, BioLegend); AF647 anti-CD86 (1:200; GL-1, BioLegend); BV605 anti-CD80 (1:200; 16-10A1, BioLegend); and BV421 anti-CD3 (1:200; 17A2, BioLegend).

Sources indicate that staining of the cell surface with fluorescently labelled antibodies and viability dyes was performed for 20 min at 4 °C in FACS buffer (PBS with 1% FCS and 2 mM EDTA). For intracellular staining of GZMB, TCF1 and Ki-67, cells were fixed and permeabilized using the True-Nuclear Transcription Factor Buffer Set (BioLegend) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Intracellular staining of CXCL9 or IL-12 was performed using the Intracellular Fixation & Permeabilization Buffer Set (Thermo Fisher) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Intracellular staining was performed overnight in permeabilization buffer at 4 °C. Flow cytometry analyses were performed using a ID7000C Spectral Cell Analyzer (ID7000 software v2.0.2.17121, Sony Biotechnologies) or a SP6800 Spectral Cell Analyzer (spectral analyser software v2.0.2.14140, Sony Biotechnologies). Flow cytometric quantification of cell numbers was done using CountBright Absolute Counting Beads (Thermo Fisher Scientific). All flow cytometric data were analysed using FlowJo (v10.10.0, BD Biosciences). Sorting of naive OT-I T cells (CD45.1+CD8+CD62L+CD44–) from blood for adoptive transfer experiments and mouse cDC1s (CD103+) from bone marrow cultures was performed using a SH800S Cell Sorter (cell sorter software v2.1.6, Sony Biotechnologies). Representative flow cytometry-gating strategies for analyses of CD8+ TILs, intratumoural cDC1s and cDC2s or splenic cDC1s and cDC2s can be found in Supplementary Fig. 1.

For adoptive transfer of OVA-specific OT-I cells, 1 × 103 congenically marked naive CD8+ T cells (CD45.1+CD8+CD62L+CD44−) were isolated from the blood of OT-I donor mice and injected intravenously into sex-matched CD45.2+ recipient mice in 100 µl sterile PBS. The transfer was performed 6 h before subcutaneous transplantation of ferroptotic control or Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− BRAF(V600E)–OVA melanoma cells.

Volumetric immunofluorescence tumour microscopy was performed as previously described45. In brief, tumours were fixed in Antigenfix solution (Diapath). Samples were dehydrated in 30% sucrose, embedded in TissueTek OCT freezing medium (Sakura Finetek) and stored at −80 °C. Consecutive sections of 50 μm thickness were generated using a Leica CM3050 S cryostat. Sections were permeabilized, blocked and stained in 0.1 M Tris (Carl Roth) supplemented with 1% BSA, 0.3% Triton X-100 (Merck), normal mouse serum (Merck) and donkey serum (Merck). Stained sections were mounted in Mowiol (Merck) and analysed using an inverted TCS SP8 confocal microscope (Leica), a STELLARIS confocal microscope (Leica) or a THUNDER imager (Leica) for tiled imaging using a HC PL APO CS2 ×20/0.75 NA objective or a HC PL APO CS2 ×40/1.30 NA THUNDER objective, or a Fluoview FV3000 microscope using an UPlanSApo ×20 air/0.75 NA objective (Olympus). All images were acquired as tiled image stacks, covering whole-tumour sections in the xy plane, with 2-μm z-spacing to provide large three-dimensional (3D) image volumes of at least 20 μm depth. Image analysis and cell rendering was performed as previously described45. 3D images were analysed using the Imaris 10.2.0 software (Oxford Instruments). The Imaris surface generation tool was used to reconstruct and visualize 3D objects for individual cells. Clusters of interacting cDC1s and CD8+ T cells were identified in a multi-step process using positional information for cell objects. CD8+ T cell clusters were defined as a minimum of five cells within a distance of 20 μm measured from the outer surface of each cell and identified using the Imaris built-in ‘distance to 5 nearest neighbours’ function. cDC1s interacting with clustered CD8+ T cells (referred to as ‘interacting cDC1’) were identified using object–object closest distance (distance ≤ 5 μm). To identify clustered CD8+ T cells interacting with cDC1s (‘interacting CD8+ T cells’), CD8+ T cells localized more than 15 μm from these interacting cDC1s were removed by distance thresholding using the Imaris filter function. Quantification of cell clusters was performed relative to the volume of the imaged section.

It has been revealed that the following antibodies were used for staining of mouse tissues: AF594 anti-CD3 (1:200; clone 17A2, BioLegend), BV421 anti-CD8α (1:100; clone 53-6.7; BioLegend), anti-CD103 (1:200; goat polyclonal; R&D Systems), FITC anti-MHC class II I-A/I-E (1:500; clone M5/114.15.2, BioLegend), AF680 anti-goat IgG (1:500; donkey polyclonal; Jackson ImmunoResearch), anti-COX2 (1:200; amino acids 584–598; Cayman Chemicals) and AF647 anti-rabbit IgG (1:400; A-21244, Invitrogen). All antibodies were either validated by the manufacturer or were previously reported for immunofluorescence microscopy.

According to recent reports, live-cell imaging was performed using a DMi8 microscope (Leica) with a HC PL APO ×20/0.8 PH2 or HC PL APO ×40/0.95 CORR PH2 objective. Temperature was regulated at 37 °C and CO2 level at 5% using a Heating Unit 2000 (Pecon) equipped with a TempController 2000 (Pecon) and CO2-Controller 2000 (Pecon). Pfa1 cells (2 × 104) were seeded in a µ-slide glass-bottom chamber slide (Ibidi) and cultivated for 24 h before imaging. Dyes for the staining of lipid peroxidation using BODIPY C11 (2 µM; Thermo Fisher Scientific), Ca2+ influx using Fluo-8-AM (4 µM; AAT Bioquest) or CalBryte 630-AM (5 µM; AAT Bioquest), small-molecule influx using FITC-labelled dextrans of 4 kDa or 70 kDa and membrane permeabilization as a marker for cell death using Sytox blue (5 µM; Thermo Fisher Scientific) or 7-AAD (1:40; Thermo Fisher Scientific) were added 30 min before imaging and kept in the media for the time of imaging. To assess lipid peroxidation by BODIPY staining, BODIPY 581/591 C11 (Thermo Fisher) was added directly into the cell culture media at a final concentration of 2 µM and cells were incubated for 30 min at 37 °C before being washed three times with PBS. For live-cell microscopy-based single-cell analyses, BODIPY C11 was kept in the media for the time of imaging. Measurement of oxidized BODIPY C11 was performed after excitation by a 488 nm laser, and measurement of non-oxidized BODIPY C11 after excitation with a 581 nm laser.

For immunohistochemistry, formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded tumour tissue sections were heated at 60 °C for 15 min and deparaffinized with xylene and graded ethanol. Sections were washed in TBS containing 0.01% Tween-20 (TBS-T) and blocked with 5% normal goat serum in TBS-T for 20 min at room temperature. Sections were then incubated overnight at 4 °C with mouse monoclonal anti-4-HNE antibody (1:200; HNEJ-2, JaICA) diluted in TBS-T containing 5% goat serum. After three washes in TBS-T, endogenous peroxidase activity was quenched by incubation with 0.3% H2O2 in methanol for 20 min, followed by three washes in TBS-T. Sections were incubated with biotinylated goat anti-mouse IgG secondary antibody (1:200; 115-065-166, Jackson ImmunoResearch) in TBS-T containing 5% goat serum for 30 min at room temperature, followed by incubation with the VECTASTAIN Elite ABC peroxidase system (PK-6100, Vector Laboratories) for 30 min at room temperature. After washing, sections were visualized using DAB substrate (SK-4100, Vector Laboratories), with development monitored microscopically until a suitable brown colour was obtained. The reaction was stopped by washing with water, and sections were counterstained with haematoxylin, blued in tap water, dehydrated through graded ethanol and xylene, and mounted in Roti Mounting medium (Carl Roth).

Generation of cDC1s was performed as previously described19, with minor modifications. In brief, bone marrow cells were isolated from mouse femur and tibia by flushing the bones with RPMI using a syringe and a 20-gauge cannula. After red blood cell lysis using ACK buffer (double-distilled H2O (ddH2O) with 150 mM ammonium chloride, 10 mM potassium bicarbonate and 1μm disodium EDTA) for 3 min at room temperature, 1.5 × 106 cells per millilitre were incubated with GM-CSF (300 pg ml−1) and FLT3L (55 ng ml−1) in RPMI 1640 medium (Thermo Fisher Scientific) supplemented with 10% FCS (PAN-Biotech), 50 µM β-mercaptoethanol (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 50 U ml–1 penicillin (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and 50 µg ml–1 streptomycin (Thermo Fisher Scientific). After 9 days of culture, non-adherent cells were reseeded at 0.3 × 106 cells per millilitre in fresh medium containing GM-CSF and FLT3L for an additional 5 days before FACS sorting of differentiated cDC1s based on CD103 expression. For assays using splenic cDCs, freshly isolated mouse spleens were digested in RPMI 1640 containing DNase I (100 µg ml–1; Merck) and collagenase IV (200 U ml–1; Thermo Fisher Scientific) for 30 min. Dendritic cells were subsequently isolated using the Pan Dendritic Cell Isolation Kit, mouse (130-100-875, Miltenyi Biotec), according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

According to recent reports, for in vitro treatment with cancer cell conditioned medium, mouse cDC1s were cultured with conditioned medium from cancer cells at 37 °C for 16 h before their analysis or use in functional assays. For assessment of cytokine and chemokine production following activation, cDC1s were stimulated with poly(I:C) (10 μg ml−1) for 4 h, and brefeldin A (5 μg ml−1) was added for the last 3 h of stimulation before proceeding with antibody staining for flow cytometric analyses. In some experiments, cDC1 stimulation was done using IFNγ (10 ng ml−1), IFNα (10 ng ml−1), 2′,3′-cGAMP (10 μM), NAD (10 μM) or ATP (100 μM). For the generation of cDC1 conditioned medium, cDC1s were first treated with cancer cell conditioned medium for 16 h, washed three times with PBS and stimulated with poly(I:C) (10 μg ml−1) for 24 h. The culture supernatant was collected and centrifuged at 600g for 5 min to remove remaining cell material, and the cell-free conditioned medium was collected and stored at −20 °C until further use.

In a recent development, to generate antigen-experienced stem-like CD8+ T cells, naive CD8+ T cells were isolated from the spleens of mice using MACS separation and stimulated with mouse anti-CD3/CD28 microbeads and IL-2 (85 U ml–1) for 4 days. After 2 days of culture, CD8+ T cells were re-seeded at 1 × 106 cells per millilitre with fresh medium containing anti-CD3/28 microbeads plus IL-2. To assess the ability of cDC1s to promote antigen-experienced CD8+ T cell expansion, 2.5 × 104 CD8+ T cells from T cell cultures were incubated with mouse anti-CD3/CD28 microbeads in the presence or absence of supernatant from cDC1s pre-treated as indicated in the figure legends. After 72 h of incubation, the number of viable CD3+CD8+ T cells was quantified by flow cytometry.

In a recent development, resazurin (7-hydroxy-10-oxidophenoxazin-10-ium-3-one, sodium; Stemcell) was added directly to the culture medium at a final concentration of 50 µg ml−1 and incubated for 1 h at 37 °C. Viability was measured at an excitation/emission wavelength of 540/590 nm using a Tecan infinite M1000Pro and Tecan i-control software (v3.9.1.0). Cell viability was calculated as the percentage of fluorescence intensity relative to the vehicle control group.

PGE2 concentration in cell-free conditioned medium was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) (Cayman Chemical) according to the manufacturer’s protocol using a Tecan infinite M1000Pro and Tecan i-control software (v3.9.1.0).

Cytokine and chemokine concentrations in conditioned medium from stimulated cDC1s were quantified using the LEGENDplex bead-based multiplex immunoassay (BioLegend) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

To block the influx of extracellular Ca2+ into ferroptotic cells, the calcium-chelator EGTA (2 mM) or the osmoprotectant PEG 3350 (10 mM) was added to the cell culture media 4 h after cancer cell treatment with the ferroptosis inducer RSL3.

Industry observers note that cells were lysed in RIPA lysis buffer (150 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA, 50 mM Tris, 1% NP-40, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate and 0.1% SDS in ddH20) containing protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Sigma-Aldrich), sonicated three times for 10 s at 35 kHz and centrifuged at 15,000g at 4 °C for 5 min. The supernatant was collected and used as the protein sample. Western blotting was performed by standard immunoblotting procedure with 12% SDS–PAGE gel and nitrocellulose membrane. Primary antibody staining to GPX4 (1:2,000; EPNCIR144, Abcam), COX2 (1:1,000; amino acids 584–598; Cayman Chemical), β-actin (1:2,000; #4967S, Cell Signaling), p38 (1:1,000; #9212S, Cell Signaling), phospho-p38 (1:1,000; D3F9, Cell Signaling), p38α (1:1,000; #9218S, Cell Signaling) or HSP60 (1:2,000; D6F1, Cell Signaling) was performed at 4 °C overnight. Horseradish peroxidase-labelled secondary antibodies to mouse IgG (1:10,000; RRID: AB_10015289, Jackson ImmunoResearch) or rabbit IgG (1:10,000; RRID: AB_2313567, Jackson ImmunoResearch) were stained for 1 h at room temperature. Bands were visualized using Pierce ECL Western Blotting Substrate (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Images were taken with a ChemiDoc XRS+ (Bio-Rad). Images were analysed with Image Lab software (v6.0.1; Bio-Rad). Images of all uncut blots can be found in Supplementary Fig. 2.

Cell-free conditioned media from cancer cells were mixed 1:1 with methanol (50% v/v) immediately after collection and stored at −80 °C. For analysis, 200 µl of each sample was thawed on ice, spiked with 10 µl of an internal standard mix (final concentration of 5 ng ml−1) and precipitated with 50 µl cold methanol (−20 °C). After protein denaturation on ice (10 min) and centrifugation (10,000g for 15 min at 4 °C), supernatants were adjusted to 1 ml with Milli-Q water. Eicosanoids were extracted using Strata-X 33-µm polymeric reversed-phase SPE plates (Phenomenex) on a Positive Pressure-96 Processor (Waters). Columns were conditioned with methanol and water, and samples were loaded and washed with 10% methanol. Target analytes were eluted in 100% methanol. Eluates were evaporated under nitrogen at 30 °C and reconstituted in 30 µl of 50% methanol. Ten microlitres were injected onto a Sciex QTRAP 6500+ mass spectrometer associated with an Exion UHPLC operated in negative-ion mode using scheduled multiple reaction monitoring. Quantification was carried out using calibration curves and internal standards, with quality control pools and blank samples analysed throughout the run to ensure accuracy and reproducibility. For BRAF(V600E), NRAS(G12D), 4T1 and MC38 cancer cell lines, fold change of each analyte production during ferroptosis relative to DMSO control group was plotted against its final concentration in ferroptotic conditioned medium. For Pfa1 cells, analytes from each oxylipin subclass (eicosanoid, hydroxylated/oxidized lipids and protectins/resolvins) were ordered from high to low abundance in ferroptotic-conditioned medium and plotted as a z-score between different treatment groups.

RNA was isolated using Monarch Total RNA Miniprep kit (New England Biolabs) and complementary DNA (cDNA) was generated using a SensiFAST cDNA synthesis kit (Bioline). Quantitative real-time PCR was performed on a LightCycler 480 (LightCycler 480 software v1.5.1, Roche) using the TAKYON No ROX SYBR MasterMix dTTP Blue kit (Eurogentec) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Gene expression was normalized to the reference gene Hprt by using the ΔCt method. All primers were purchased from Eurofins.

In vitro-generated WT or ItgaxcrePtger2−/−Ptger4fl/fl CD103+ cDC1s were incubated for 16 h with conditioned medium from control or Ptgs1/Ptgs2−/− ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) melanoma cells followed by stimulation with poly(I:C) (10 μg ml−1) for an additional 4 h. RNA was isolated using an Arcturus PicoPure RNA isolation kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Library preparation was carried out using the Novogene manufactured internal kit. mRNA was purified from total RNA using poly-T oligo-attached magnetic beads. After fragmentation, the first strand cDNA was synthesized using random hexamer primers, followed by the second strand cDNA synthesis using dUTP for directional (strand-specific) library construction. Sequencing was performed on a NovaSeq X Plus with 25B flowcell 2 × 150 bp paired-end sequencing (300 cycles kit). The raw fastq files related to the sequence reads were mapped to the mouse genome, which was downloaded from the UCSC browser (GRCm38/mm10), using the STAR algorithm46. The reads were counted using the Rsubread R package47. These read counts were normalized, and differentially expressed genes were analysed using the iDEP (v2.01) web server48, utilizing the DESeq2 R package49 for differentially expressed gene identification (with fold change ≥ 1.5 and adjusted P < 0.05). Principal component analysis was performed using the prcomp R function and plotted using the ggplot2 R package. Volcano plots were rendered using the Enhanced Volcano R package (https://github.com/kevinblighe/EnhancedVolcano). The ‘Core functional cDC1’ gene set was defined as activation-induced genes significantly downregulated in activated cDC1s following incubation with conditioned medium from ferroptotic control BRAF(V600E) cells. Hierarchical clustering of core functional cDC1 genes was performed using the hclust function in R (Euclidean distance, complete linkage), and heatmaps were generated using the heatmap.2 function of the gplots R package. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was performed on core functional cDC1 genes and arranged according to log2(fold changes). Enrichment of gene sets was then conducted using GSEA (v4.2.3)50. Gene sets related to cytokine signalling and cell migration were extracted from the Molecular Signature Database (https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/index.jsp). Gene signatures for antigen uptake and cross-presentation were from a previous study51. The gene set for PGE2 impaired functional cDC1 genes was from a previous study19. PGE2-impaired core functional cDC1 genes for correlation analysis were defined as activation-induced genes significantly downregulated in activated cDC1s following incubation with PGE2. The PreRanked tool from GSEA (v4.2.3) was used to assess the normalized enrichment score, and a false discovery rate (q < 0.25) was utilized to evaluate the statistical significance of the normalized enrichment score.

Industry observers note that throughout this study, different statistical tests were used to assess statistical significance, as indicated in the figure legends. Data are shown as the mean ± s.e.m., mean ± minimum and maximum values or boxplots, as indicated in the figure legends.

Data shown in Figs. 1e and 3g are pooled from two independent experiments. Data shown in Figs. 1b,d, 2b,c,h–k,m–q, 3f,i and 4d,g are representative of two independent experiments. For the boxplots in Figs. 1b, 2h–k,m–o and 3i, the centre line indicates the mean and the bounds show the minimum and maximum values. For the boxplots in Figs. 1e and 4c,e,f,h,i,k, the centre line indicates the median, the bounds extend from the 25th to 75th percentiles and the whiskers correspond to the minimum and maximum values. GraphPad Prism software (v9.5.0 and v9.5.1) was used for statistical analyses.

a-d, Quantification of PGE2 production in cancer cells upon genetic ablation of Gpx4. Gpx4−/− BRAFV600E melanoma cells (a), Gpx4−/− LLC lung cancer cells (b) and Gpx4−/− MC38 colorectal cancer cells (c) were deprived of the lipid peroxidation inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) to induce ferroptosis and PGE2 production was measured 24 h later (n = 3 samples). d, Measurement of PGE2 production by CreERT2 Gpx4fl/fl small cell lung cancer (SCLC) cells after treatment with or without 4-hydroxy-tamoxifen (4-OHT) for 72 h (n = 3 samples). e,f, Measurement of PGE2 production in NRASG12D melanoma (e) or 4T1 breast cancer (f) cells treated with the ferroptosis inducers RSL3, ML210 or Erastin (n = 3 samples). g, PGE2 production by human HT-29 cells treated with RSL3 or Necrocide-1 (NC1) for 24 h. (n = 3 samples). h, Analysis of PGE2 production in MC38 cells treated with necroptosis-inducing combination of TNFα, LCL-161 and Emricasan for 24 h (n = 4 samples). Data in a-f are representative of two independent experiments. Centre of box plots in a-f indicate the mean with bounds showing the minimum and maximum values. Bar graphs in g indicate mean ± s.e.m. Data in h are depicted as box plots extending from the 25th to 75th percentiles with the median as the centre and the whiskers corresponding to the minimum and maximum values. P-values in a-d, h are from unpaired Student’s t-tests (two-sided), P-values in e-g are from one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparison test (two-sided). NS, not significant (P ≥ 0.05).

It has been revealed that a,b, Measurement of PGE2 production (a) and cell viability (b) for indicated cancer cell lines treated with the ferroptosis inducer RSL3 with or without inhibition of lipid peroxidation by liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1), caspase inhibition (z-VAD-FMK) or RIPK1 inhibition (Nec-1S) for 24 h (n = 3 samples). c-e, Effect of RSL3-mediated ferroptosis induction on PGE2 production for indicated (c) mouse and (d) human cancer cells (MC38, 4T1, LLC, CT26, PancO2, NRASG12D, D4M.3 A, PDAC #10158, PDAC #53578, PDAC # 6075, PDAC #4888, Su86.86, PDAC #1, PDAC #2, PDAC #3, PDAC #4, A549, HT-29, n = 3 samples; BRAFV600E, n = 7 samples; SCLC #Rp181.5, n = 4 samples; SCLC #278.3, n = 2 samples). e, Plot showing the relative increase in PGE2 production induced by RSL3-mediated ferroptosis across mouse and human cancer cells from c and d (MC38, 4T1, LLC, CT26, PancO2, NRASG12D, D4M.3 A, PDAC #10158, PDAC #53578, PDAC # 6075, PDAC #4888, Su86.86, PDAC #1, PDAC #2, PDAC #3, PDAC #4, A549, HT-29, n = 3 samples; BRAFV600E, n = 7 samples; SCLC #Rp181.5, n = 4 samples; SCLC #278.3, n = 2 samples). Data in a-e are representative of two independent experiments. Centre of box plots in a,c,d indicate the mean with bounds showing the minimum and maximum values. a, Quantification of CXCL9 production in cDC1s exposed to PGE2 (100 ng/ml) or conditioned medium (CM) from ferroptotic control BRAFV600E cells treated with the ferroptosis inducers RSL3 or ML210 for (n = 4 samples). b,c, cDC1s were treated with cancer cell CM as indicated, stimulated with poly I:C and analysed for IL-12 production by intracellular staining. b, Representative flow cytometry plots showing IL-12 expression. c, Quantification of IL-12+ cDC1s, based on b (n = 4 samples). d, Effect of PGE2 or CM from ferroptotic BRAFV600E cells on CXCL9 production in splenic cDC1s and cDC2s, measured after intracellular staining by flow cytometry (n = 6 samples). e, Effect of PGE2 or CM from ferroptotic BRAFV600E cells on chemokine and cytokine production by poly I:C-activated cDC1s, measured in the culture supernatant by bead-based flow cytometric analyses (n = 6 samples). f-h, Analysis of cDC1s by RNA-seq (n = 4). f, Venn diagram showing the overlap between core functional cDC1 genes inhibited by factors derived from ferroptotic cancer cells (Ferroptosis CM) and synthetic PGE2. g, Correlation analysis of core functional cDC1 genes regulated by PGE2 and ferroptotic cancer cell CM. h, GSEA of pathways linked to cDC1 functions in cDC1s exposed to ferroptotic cancer cell CM. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All credit to this young man, who has opened up on the reality of being excluded from Nuno’s West Ham squad. Particularly so at a time when criticism of another Nuno cast-off, Alphonse Areola, is flying around as Areola is apparently needed but not ready for Scott Parkers’ West Ham relaunch.

Ezra Mayers, invisible for months and on the fringes of the Hammers squad, seemingly unable to influence his manager, is suddenly thrust back into the spotlight after replacing Nuno’s choice Morato at left back during new manager Scott Parker’s first game in the dugout.

“It’s been really, really tough, going through the months not playing, not being in the squad. It was a case of making sure I stick at it and having the mentality to come in every day and still improve and perform when I couldn’t really see any opportunities coming my way.

That is definitely something that I’ve had to learn.

Nuno Espírito Santo apparently left out many from his ‘match day squad’ with whom he concentrated – Mayers was one who found it tough going.

And on the call from fresh manager Scott Parker which has thrust him back into first team contention:.

Industry observers note that “I’ve been given an opportunity now and it’s been really good. The world works for you sometimes and I’m definitely going to give it my all and stake my claim to become a part of the team.”.

One of several young, talented players who’d become invisible under Nuno – Scarles and Ajala included – Ezra Mayers serves as a brilliant example of one who didn’t let his standards slip even whilst out of the team and the reckoning.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 13:32, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 13:34.
  • Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Sunday, when they head to Estadio El Sadar to tackle Osasuna.
  • The White and Sky Blues are the only team in Spain's top flight yet to triumph this term, and they are in danger of becoming cut adrift at the bottom of the La Liga table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 13:32, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 13:34.

Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Sunday, when they head to Estadio El Sadar to tackle Osasuna.

The White and Sky Blues are the only team in Spain's top flight yet to triumph this term, and they are in danger of becoming cut adrift at the bottom of the La Liga table.

Osasuna boast a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 16th spot in the division.

Jagoba Arrasate's side entered the November international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Athletic Bilbao, but they did start the month with a 2-1 loss to Deportivo La Coruna.

The Little Reds finished 17th in Spain's top flight last season, level on points with 18th-placed Mallorca, only surviving on head-to-head points.

As a result, there is plenty of room for improvement during the current campaign, but consistency has been a problem in the opening months of the season.

Osasuna have only won seven of their previous 32 matches against Malaga in all competitions, suffering 12 defeats in the process, while there have also been 13 draws.

Malaga are winless in their last four games against Osasuna, though, and they have beaten Sunday's opponents just once since April 2013.

This match will mark the first fixture between the two teams since March 2019, when Osasuna recorded a 2-1 victory, while they also won 2-1 in the reverse game in the same season.

Malaga are rock bottom of the La Liga table, only picking up five points from their opening 12 matches of the season, boasting a record of zero wins, five draws and seven defeats.

Juan Francisco Funes' side entered the November international break off the back of successive defeats to Real Betis and Racing de Santander.

Los Albicelestes also have the joint-second worst defensive record in La Liga this season with 23 goals conceded, while they have the second-worst attack with only nine goals scored.

Osasuna form (all competitions):.

Malaga form (all competitions):.

Osasuna need to make late checks on Aimar Oroz, Jorge Herrando and Romain Del Castillo before final decisions on the trio can be made.

There are not expected to be any surprises in the Osasuna XI for this match, with Ante Budimir again set to lead the line; the experienced striker has eight goals in 12 appearances this term.

Ruben Garcia and Raul Moro are also expected to feature in the final third of the field, while there should be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Lucas Torro.

As for Malaga, Adam Aznou is suspended following his red card against Racing last time out.

Juan Cruz, Julen Lobete, Diego Murillo, Aaron Ochoa and Carlos Puga are also expected to be absent for the away side due to injury problems.

Adrian Nino has scored five times in eight appearances this season, and the 22-year-old will again feature in the final third of the field for the White and Sky Blues.

Osasuna possible starting lineup:.

Fernandez; Rosier, Boyomo, Catena, Bretones; Moncayola, Torro, Gomez; Ruben Garcia, Budimir, Moro.

Malaga possible starting lineup:.

Herrero; Larrubia, Calero, Pastor, Galilea; Dotor, Enriquez, Rodriguez, Lorenzo; Nino, Chupe.

We are expecting Malaga's winless run to continue this weekend, but the visitors have enough quality to secure a share of the spoils against an inconsistent Osasuna.

Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.
  • Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.
  • Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Recent findings suggest that verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

According to recent reports, verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

According to recent reports, verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a major statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

In a recent development, verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

It has been revealed that verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very vital.

Sources indicate that that brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:.

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Recent findings suggest that some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

Industry observers note that there is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format presently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

Industry observers note that the draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He claims if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Recent findings suggest that marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”.

In a recent development, up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Recent findings suggest that marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the major screen in the background.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Industry observers note that proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the upcoming format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the Champions League draw in Monaco, with the 36 teams in this season’s competition finding out their eight league phase fixtures.

The teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal will be among the teams joining the Parisians in pot one, while the two remaining English teams, Manchester United and Aston Villa, will be in pot two.

Sources indicate that proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

This season is the third under the upcoming format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

Recent findings suggest that for example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

Hull City vs. Brighton: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.
  • Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.
  • Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.

Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.

Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.

Conversely, the Seagulls arrive full of confidence after recording consecutive top-flight wins over Manchester City and Brentford, boasting six clean sheets across their last seven league outings.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Hull and Brighton.

Nearly 67 years have passed since Hull City and Brighton & Hove Albion first locked horns - a November 1959 Division Two clash that ended in a 3-1 victory for the Tigers - and there have now been 51 competitive meetings between the two clubs in all competitions.

The Seagulls hold the bragging rights when it comes to overall victories with 22, while Hull have claimed 15 wins of their own and another 14 contests have seen the spoils shared.

Remarkably, none of those 51 encounters have taken place in the Premier League, with every previous battle arriving in the Football League or the FA Cup, and the two sides have not crossed paths since a goalless Championship stalemate in East Yorkshire in February 2016.

Recent clashes between the pair have been notably tight, low-scoring affairs, with none of their last nine meetings across all competitions settled by more than a single goal and three ending 0-0.

During the 2015-16 campaign, both clubs collected a narrow 1-0 victory on home soil - Brighton prevailing in the Championship in September 2015 before Hull gained revenge in the FA Cup four months later - prior to that goalless draw in February.

Indeed, home advantage has heavily dictated this fixture in the modern era, as Hull are unbeaten in their last six home games against Brighton across all competitions - winning four and keeping five clean sheets - since suffering a 2-0 Division Three defeat in October 2000.

Conversely, the Tigers have endured a miserable record on the South Coast, failing to win any of their last 22 visits to Brighton since recording their sole away triumph in this fixture - a 2-1 Division Three success - way back in August 1965.

Brighton built much of their overall head-to-head lead during a dominant spell in the late 1980s and 1990s, rattling off four straight victories between October 1989 and April 1991 before later embarking on a nine-match unbeaten run from April 1993 to December 1996.

That sequence included the Seagulls' biggest-ever win in this matchup, a resounding 4-0 Division Two triumph in March 1996, while they also completed a comfortable league double over Hull with 2-0 and 3-0 victories in the 2000-01 Division Three season.

Hull's most emphatic triumph came in the highest-scoring meeting between the two sides, a 5-2 Division Two victory in December 1988, while they also put three unanswered goals past Brighton in March 1997.

The two teams have also collided five times in the FA Cup, with Brighton winning the first two ties in January 1985 (1-0) and January 1986 (3-2) before Hull turned the tide by edging a 2-1 replay victory in February 2014 following a 1-1 draw and claiming that 1-0 success in January 2016.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Sources indicate that other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham’s familiar profligacy in front of goal came back to haunt them, as did their propensity to go behind in the first half of games as the points were shared at London Stadium this afternoon.

From Preston’s first corner, the fanbase was understandably apprehensive, knowing West Ham’s weaknesses from dead balls earlier in the season. Again the curse struck, with Piroe heading the ball over his own oncoming goal keeper’s fists, the ball then looping onto the post and allowing a gentle tap-in for Preston to take the lead.

Herrick rallied well after conceding early.

The wheels could have come off for West Ham’s young goal keeper at that point: However, all credit to Herrick. It would have been very easy for his confidence to crumble after that early combi-cock-up, but he rallied well and even appeared to be smiling as the game went on, with several catches and a couple of really good saves surely meaning the shirt is his for the time being.

West Ham hit the post four times during a frenetic period in the first half when their intensity was high, but it seemed as though the ball simply would not go between the posts.

Recent findings suggest that familiar problems surfaced in the second half as the pace dropped and West Ham ran out of ideas, notably after Austbø had been substituted. Manor Solomon, looking very one-footed, simply ran inside and passed square. Frustratingly, the game slowed in pace in the last twenty minutes with the Hammers looking devoid of newly introduced ideas just at the time when they should have been upping the tempo.

It is clear that there’s still a shortage of pace in this side and with a build up that got slower as the game went on, West Ham’s bench looked as if it desperately needed an injection of Antonio-like pace to scare opponents and perhaps take on a shot!

In a recent development, A disappointment for the West Ham supporters, who booed their team off in the now time-honoured tradition as another two points went west. Against the bottom side.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

In a recent development, they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under latest manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

Industry observers note that city created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Sources indicate that erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

According to recent reports, however, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

Industry observers note that he mentioned: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

According to recent reports, rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

In a recent development, erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the latest Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Industry observers note that sage remarked: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

It has been revealed that “It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

According to recent reports, “We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ.

According to recent reports, "Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ.

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

There will be five added minutes.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

In a recent development, cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

In a recent development, erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

In a recent development, there is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Industry observers note that palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Industry observers note that sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

According to recent reports, three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

It has been revealed that rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

Pino is lining up the free-kick...

Sources indicate that the next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Sources indicate that semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

In a recent development, we are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

No changes for either side at the break.

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

In a recent development, palace now miss a major opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Recent findings suggest that foden wastes his second significant chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Sources indicate that well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl.

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

According to recent reports, there is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Sources indicate that quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Industry observers note that manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

In a recent development, we are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

In a recent development, both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Sources indicate that crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

According to recent reports, “He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

Industry observers note that “That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”.

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY.

It has been revealed that jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.
